title: EXP-031 — Select Form Retained-Filter Refresh Semantics
objective: In one artifact-read-only experiment against the existing live Web Client, characterize whether Select Form retains and applies an exact Name filter after ordinary dialog Cancel and reopen. First use known-existing `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02` as the positive control: with Filter By=Name, Case Sensitive unchecked, and Starts With unchecked, set the exact filter, Cancel the dialog, reopen Select Form once, and inspect the retained text/settings and settled rendered row. Only if the positive control passes, test `FX_SelectFormFilterProbe01` as a proposed absence-probe string that this experiment must never create: set its exact filter, Cancel, reopen once, and inspect the retained text/settings and visible case-insensitive matches. Do not assume database absence from the name or repository history. Screenshots/accessibility observations are decisive; naturally available request/response evidence is corroboration only. UI filter changes and dialog lifecycle actions are permitted, but no Web Client or Designer Form may be opened, closed, edited, saved, or created. A successful first execution is observed only; independent replay is needed before verifying this preflight procedure.

Preserve all existing Web Client and Designer Form state without mutation

Use the supported Web Client Select Form dialog only; record whether it is already open. If closed, permit one initial Open solely to enter the test; if already open, use it without an extra lifecycle reset. Record the inherited filter/settings before changing them

Establish Filter By=Name with Case Sensitive and Starts With visibly unchecked before the first tested Cancel. On each tested reopen, inspect retained filter text/settings before any further input; if they are not retained, record that outcome without repairing or refilling the reopened dialog
Use existing `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02` only as a known-present positive control
Use `FX_SelectFormFilterProbe01` only as a proposed absence-probe string; it must never be created by this experiment and must not be presumed absent from the database
For the positive-control sequence: set the exact Name filter, ordinarily Cancel Select Form, reopen Select Form exactly once, and inspect the newly settled rendered result

Proceed to the absence-probe sequence only after the positive-control retained-filter result passes: set the exact probe Name filter, Cancel, reopen Select Form exactly once, and inspect the retained text/settings and settled rendered result. If the positive-control check fails, stop without starting this second sequence
Capture rendered screenshots/accessibility snapshots identifying filter text, Filter By, Case Sensitive state, and settled row result
Capture relevant Select Form request/response evidence if naturally available, as corroboration only
Use at most one fresh snapshot plus one corrected visible inspection if a reopened result is ambiguous

Inspection recovery permits no further filter input or dialog lifecycle attempt. After the last permitted inspection, allow one final ordinary Cancel solely to dismiss the test dialog without another reopen; record the retained filter and final browser/Form state. Do not restore the filter through another test sequence
Write evidence only under `evidence/EXP-031/` and the EXP-031 experiment record

artifacts: FX_SelectFormFilterProbe01 (absence-probe name only; must not be created)

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence proves a usable live Web Client Select Form workflow, records inherited Form state plus whether the dialog is open and its current filter/settings, and preserves inherited Web Client/Designer Forms untouched. If the dialog is closed, at most one initial Open is permitted solely to enter the test. Record that no Mongoose artifact mutation, Form activation, Save, Regenerate, unload, User Preference change, or session-establishment action occurred. If no usable existing workflow is available, stop blocked without authenticating or recreating it.

Before the positive-control Cancel, evidence shows exact filter `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02`, Filter By=Name, Case Sensitive unchecked, and Starts With unchecked. After exactly one tested Select Form reopen and before further input, evidence must show that exact filter and settings retained and a settled rendered row whose Name equals `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02`. Filter text alone or an unrelated/stale row is insufficient. If the text/settings are not retained or the expected row cannot be established within one fresh snapshot plus one corrected visible inspection, record the result, fail this check, and stop without the absence-probe sequence, refilling, or further lifecycle retry.

Only after AC-2 passes, set the exact probe filter `FX_SelectFormFilterProbe01` with Filter By=Name, Case Sensitive unchecked, and Starts With unchecked, then Cancel and perform exactly one tested reopen. Before further input, evidence must show the same exact filter/settings retained and a settled rendered result with zero visible case-insensitive Name matches. If the filter/settings are not retained, matching rows appear, or the result remains stale/ambiguous within the bounded inspection, record that result and stop without correction or another lifecycle attempt. Any zero-match finding is limited to this inspected UI result; the probe must not be presumed absent from the database.

For a successful full execution, reconcile exactly two filter-setting operations, two tested Cancels, and two tested reopens: first the positive control, then the probe. Separately account for at most one initial Open if the dialog began closed and at most one final Cancel solely to dismiss the test dialog, with no further reopen. Snapshot/corrected-inspection recovery authorizes no extra filter input or lifecycle retry. If stopped early, record actual counts and unperformed steps rather than claiming both sequences completed. No Enter, OK, row activation, or Form open/close is permitted.

Final repository and action audit proves changes are confined to the EXP-031 record plus `evidence/EXP-031/`, no Mongoose artifacts were created/modified or Forms activated, and inherited Form state was preserved. Record the final dialog state and retained filter without performing an extra reset. A successful first execution is observed Select Form retained-filter/reopen behavior in the tested 2026.09.08 environment, not a verified preflight procedure. An independent clean replay is required before verification; failed/unresolved checks remain recorded as such without database absence/uniqueness claims.

notes: Proposed after blocked run R-20261007-195234-KQJh. EXP-030 confirmed the rendered positive control but could not establish target absence: changing/refilling the Name filter in an already-open Select Form dialog left stale rows. EXP-028 and EXP-029 also completed blocked at preflight; EXP-028 supplied a partial exact-target zero-row observation, not an accepted complete preflight. This separate experiment permits a distinct dialog-lifecycle sequence that EXP-030 could not use as recovery: set an exact filter, Cancel normally, reopen once, and inspect whether both the filter/settings and corresponding rendered result are retained/applied. Test the known-existing positive control first and the proposed zero-match probe only if that passes. Do not press Enter/OK or activate rows, because prior observations show those actions can open a Web Client Form. Document initial/final dialog actions separately from the two tested reopens. Success provides one observed candidate preflight procedure; only a later independent clean replay could verify it. No blocked run is repaired or resumed, no Mongoose artifact is created, and no Form/component recovery or database claim is made.
